quality_assessment: Chapter provides excellent introductory content with accurate examples, but misses some important features available in ripgrep that would benefit beginners

issues.description: Chapter doesn't explain regex engine selection with --engine flag
issues.should_add: Document --engine flag options: default (Rust regex-automata), pcre2, auto
issues.fix_suggestion: Add subsection 'Regex Engine Selection' explaining default DFA-based engine vs PCRE2, with --engine flag usage and when to switch engines

issues.description: Named capture groups syntax not documented despite being supported
issues.should_be: Show both numbered and named capture syntax: (?P<name>...)
issues.fix_suggestion: Add example showing named captures: rg '(?P<level>error|warning): (?P<msg>.+)' to demonstrate the syntax available

issues.description: Default regex engine limitations not explained (no backreferences, possessive quantifiers, atomic groups)
issues.should_add: Add note explaining what regex features require PCRE2: backreferences, lookahead/lookbehind, possessive quantifiers, atomic groups
issues.fix_suggestion: Add 'Default Engine Limitations' subsection explaining: 'ripgrep's default Rust regex engine doesn't support backreferences, lookahead/lookbehind, or atomic groups. Use -P/--pcre2 for these features.'

issues.description: Multiline mode flag -U mentioned but not --multiline-dotall flag
issues.should_add: Document --multiline-dotall flag which makes . match newlines in multiline mode
issues.fix_suggestion: In a future 'Advanced Patterns' chapter, explain --multiline-dotall usage with -U flag

issues.description: Unicode character classes mentioned briefly but comprehensive list not provided
issues.should_be: Expand to show Unicode character classes: \p{L} (letters), \p{N} (numbers), \p{P} (punctuation), \p{Ll} (lowercase), \p{Lu} (uppercase), \P{...} for negation
issues.fix_suggestion: Add subsection 'Unicode Character Classes' with table showing common \p{} classes and examples like: rg '\p{L}+' for Unicode letters

issues.description: PCRE2 mentioned only in passing, but not when/why to use it
issues.current_content: Brief mention in Groups and Alternation section
issues.should_be: Dedicated subsection explaining -P/--pcre2 flag, when to use it (backreferences, lookahead/lookbehind), and performance tradeoffs
issues.fix_suggestion: Add 'PCRE2 Engine' subsection explaining: 'Use -P flag for Perl-compatible regex features like backreferences (\1), lookahead (?=...), and lookbehind (?<=...). Example: rg -P "(\w+)\s+\1" finds repeated words.'

issues.description: Chapter doesn't mention the underlying regex library used (regex-automata)
issues.should_add: Brief note that ripgrep uses Rust's regex-automata library for default engine
issues.fix_suggestion: Add technical note: 'ripgrep uses the regex-automata library (DFA-based) for its default engine, providing excellent performance for most patterns.'

positive_aspects: Excellent progressive structure from simple to complex patterns
All flag examples are accurate and work as documented
Good coverage of basic metacharacters and character classes
Helpful 'Common Mistakes' section addresses real user issues
Comprehensive cheat sheet table for quick reference
Word and line boundary matching well explained with -w and -x flags
Output format sections cover heading vs non-heading modes well
Context lines (-A, -B, -C) explained with clear examples
Inverted matching with -v flag covered with practical examples
improvement_suggestions: Add 'Regex Engine Selection' subsection explaining --engine flag and default vs PCRE2
Expand 'Unicode Character Classes' section with comprehensive \p{} examples
Add dedicated PCRE2 subsection explaining when/why to use -P flag
Add note about default engine limitations to set proper expectations
Consider adding subsection on regex performance (literal extraction optimization)
Link to 'Advanced Patterns' chapter for multiline and PCRE2 deep-dive
Add troubleshooting tip: 'If pattern requires backreferences or lookahead, use -P flag'

metadata.validation_focus: Verify examples of basic search patterns and regex syntax with working examples
